scope: Theorem 11.7 (The full accuracy range by predecessor-span localization) of the manuscript “Localization costs and information growth for exact Gaussian observations” (preprints/Localization-costs-and-information-growth-for-exact-Gaussian-observations-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f43e1443f9fd513), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 78. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M(d) = o(d2) be integer-valued and let 0 < ϵ(d) ≤ 1/10. A family of learners in Section 2 whose angular success probability is at least 2/3 for a uniform spherical signal must use T(d) ≥ c d log(1/ϵ(d)) for all sufficiently large d, where c > 0 is absolute. The eventual threshold may depend on the memory sequence. The same conclusion follows from success at least 2/3 for every fixed signal.
